name: The Tribune building
address: Southeast corner of Madison and Dearborn Streets

status.today: Later buildings stand on the corner
status.note: It burned on 9 October 1871. The corner's later buildings are not researched here.

built.note: The paper moved into its new building at the end of the 1860s (Andreas vol. 2, p. 492; the year is damaged in the scan read).

summary: The Chicago Tribune's own building, four storeys of Joliet marble with iron frames and roof. People thought it could not burn. At four in the morning it was the only newspaper office still standing, but it burned after daylight.

notable.text: The entrance is on the cut-off corner, under the paper's name.
It had iron shutters and was called 'absolutely fireproof'.
Its stone walls still stood after the fire.

story.text: The Tribune moves to Madison and Dearborn.
The fireproof building burns after daylight.
